notice.title: Prototype transparency
notice.text: This mockup currently reads static JSON files. In the production portal, every metric and AI-assisted answer will identify its connected source, selected scope, calculation version and last successful refresh.

principles.title: Source first
principles.text: Every number names its authoritative source and shows when that source was last refreshed.

principles.title: Calculation visible
principles.text: Definitions, formulas, exclusions and active filters are available beside the metric.

principles.title: Evidence-linked AI
principles.text: AI explains approved portal data and cites the records used; it does not invent missing results.

principles.title: Project insight only
principles.text: Signals support teams and delivery planning. They are never individual performance scores.

metrics.name: Manual test baseline
metrics.definition: The distinct active manual test cases in Zephyr for the selected team, application and period. For this portal, the manual baseline represents 100% of the agreed test requirement coverage.
metrics.formula: Count of distinct active Zephyr manual test cases

metrics.name: Automated manual cases
metrics.definition: Distinct manual cases linked in Zephyr to at least one active automation test. One automation test may cover several manual cases; each manual case is counted once.
metrics.formula: Distinct manual case IDs with an active automation link

metrics.name: Automation coverage
metrics.definition: The share of the manual test baseline that has a valid automation mapping in Zephyr.
metrics.formula: Automated manual cases ÷ manual test baseline × 100
metrics.exclusions: Manual cases outside the active baseline

metrics.name: Manual-only percentage
metrics.definition: The portion of the manual baseline that does not yet have a valid automation mapping.
metrics.formula: (Manual baseline − automated manual cases) ÷ manual baseline × 100

metrics.name: Smoke test percentage
metrics.definition: The share of active automation tests classified as smoke. Other automated tests are treated as regression unless explicitly excluded.
metrics.formula: Active smoke automation tests ÷ active automation tests × 100

metrics.name: Pass rate
metrics.definition: Successful completed automated executions in the selected period. The portal keeps first-run pass rate separate from final pass rate after retries.
metrics.formula: Passed completed executions ÷ all completed executions × 100

metrics.name: Flaky execution rate
metrics.definition: The percentage of executed tests whose outcome changes across retries or comparable recent runs. The configured detection rule and period will be shown with the metric.
metrics.formula: Tests meeting the flakiness rule ÷ executed automated tests × 100
metrics.source: Normalized CI results in portal database
metrics.exclusions: Known environment outages and manually cancelled runs

metrics.name: Open blockers
metrics.definition: Unresolved Jira QA blockers and blocked Zephyr cycles in the selected scope. Linked records are deduplicated.

metrics.name: Manual time saved estimate
metrics.definition: An estimate of manual execution time avoided by successful automation runs. It is a project planning estimate, not a measure of individual productivity.
metrics.formula: Successful automated executions × approved manual duration estimate
metrics.exclusions: Failed runs, setup time and unapproved estimates

metrics.name: UFT migration completion
metrics.definition: Progress moving the identified UFT inventory to SandsARC, with migrated tests counted only after validation or approved retirement.
metrics.formula: (Validated + retired cases) ÷ identified UFT migration scope × 100
metrics.exclusions: New SandsARC-only tests outside migration scope

metrics.name: Runs in period
metrics.definition: Accepted workflow and pipeline run records, whether launched from this portal or scheduled directly in GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps.
metrics.formula: Count of unique normalized run IDs in the selected period
metrics.exclusions: Duplicate webhook events and rejected test records

metrics.name: Release readiness
metrics.definition: A transparent project-level status based on agreed QA exit criteria, test completion and unresolved blockers. It is not an AI-generated score or an employee KPI.
metrics.formula: Ready, At risk or Blocked using the displayed project rules

metrics.name: QA effort by activity
metrics.definition: Jira worklogs and estimates grouped by team, project and activity such as planning, execution, automation and defect support.
metrics.formula: Sum of approved effort records by activity
metrics.exclusions: Personal ranking, utilization scoring and non-QA work

metrics.name: Capacity support signal
metrics.definition: A coordination view of open work, remaining estimates and blockers that helps identify where assistance or rebalancing may be useful.
metrics.formula: Displayed inputs only; no composite performance score
metrics.exclusions: Performance ratings, productivity rankings and hidden scoring

sources.name: Zephyr
sources.role: Test inventory and traceability source of truth

sources.name: Jira
sources.role: Work, release and blocker source of truth

sources.name: GitHub
sources.freshness: Planned: on change and daily check

sources.name: Portal database
data: Run requests, settings and AI evidence metadata

lineage.title: Source systems
lineage.text: Zephyr, Jira, GitHub, GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps

lineage.title: Connectors
lineage.text: Read-only APIs, webhooks, service hooks and scheduled reconciliation

lineage.title: Validation
lineage.text: Schema checks, identity mapping, deduplication and quality rules

lineage.title: Portal database
lineage.text: Normalized results, source references, configuration and trend snapshots

lineage.title: Metric service
lineage.text: Versioned formulas apply the selected team, application and period

lineage.title: Portal and AI
lineage.text: Dashboards display the metric; AI explains it with the same evidence

stored: Application and team catalog with external source identifiers
Normalized execution results and links to CI artifacts
Versioned metric snapshots used for weekly, monthly and yearly trends
Portal run requests, approved schedules, favorites and notification status
Connector sync health, checkpoints, validation errors and correlation IDs
AI question context, evidence references, citations and audit metadata
notStored: Integration credentials or secrets in readable form
Private email bodies unrelated to portal notifications
Individual performance ratings, rankings or hidden productivity scores

steps.title: Understand the question
steps.text: The portal includes the current page, selected team, application, period and referenced metric.

steps.title: Choose approved data
steps.text: The AI uses read-only portal tools that expose only permitted metrics and source-linked records.

steps.title: Retrieve evidence
steps.text: It retrieves calculated metrics and the supporting Zephyr, Jira or CI references from the portal database.

steps.title: Explain, not recalculate
steps.text: The model summarizes, compares and highlights patterns; authoritative calculations remain in the versioned metric service.

steps.title: Show the trail
steps.text: The answer displays citations, freshness, active filters, assumptions and any missing or delayed data.

can: Explain a metric in plain language
Summarize release risks and test results
Highlight anomalies and suggest the next investigation
Draft a test-run configuration for human review
cannot: Invent or silently fill missing source data
Change metric definitions or override source results
Rank people or infer individual performance
Trigger a pipeline, send email or update Jira without confirmation
Bypass portal access rules or reveal secrets

example.question: Why did automation coverage rise this month?
example.evidence: Coverage snapshots, Zephyr mapping changes, selected team and date range
example.calculation: The metric service compares distinct automated manual cases against the manual baseline
example.answer: AI explains the cases added or removed, links to the relevant mappings and states any sync delay

governance.title: Initial visibility
governance.text: During the initial phase everyone can view every section. The planned model has All QA access and Management access.

governance.title: Responsible use
governance.text: Metrics describe projects and QA teams. Individual Jira details are used only to coordinate support and capacity.

governance.title: Freshness and ownership
governance.text: Production views will show last successful refresh, source owner, metric owner and calculation version.

governance.title: Corrections
governance.text: Users will be able to report a questionable metric, see validation issues and follow the correction status.
